learning_outcomes.text: Students should have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
Students should have developed those learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.

Students should know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated by the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their area of study.
Applied knowledge of manufacturing systems and processes, metrology and quality control.
Ability to work, lead and manage conflicts in a multidisciplinary group and/or a multilingual environment.
Ability to apply new technologies, including information and communication technologies.
Ability to manage information, handle and apply technical specifications and legislation necessary for the practice of engineering.

syllabus_topics: Introduction and objectives of Industrial Maintenance Plan
Product control and liability for damages caused
RUE-2023/1230 on Machinery. Scope of application
Introduction to Conformity Assessment and Machine Adaptation
Adaptation of used machines and equipment
Introduction to Risk Assessment in Machines
Functional safety of machines and equipment
Maintenance Plan for an industrial activity
teaching_methods: Expository classes in large groups (lectures, theoretical exposition, general examples, conferences)
Small group classes (practical activities, computer labs, laboratories, seminars, presentations, debates)
Collective tutorials (clarification of doubts, supervision of assignments)

assessment_methods.method: Attendance and participation in face-to-face and/or virtual activities
Theory exam (continuous assessment partial tests and/or a final exam)

assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 0.15 for attendance and participation (S1) + 0.55 for the theory exam (S2) + 0.3 for practical and directed assignments (S3). It is essential to complete the theory exam, attend practical sessions, and submit proposed assignments to pass the course. To pass the course, a minimum score of 5 out of 10 must be achieved on both the theory exam and the proposed practical assignments and work.
